conventions.convention: K(θ)=KL(P0‖Pθ) is directional; its attained minimum K* is finite, Θ* contains all minimizers, and Bε={θ:K(θ)−K*≤ε}.

The metric parameter space carries its Borel sigma-algebra; finite-valued normalized density representatives are supplied jointly measurably relative to one sigma-finite dominating measure. AC is inherited through the likelihood-density and KL conventions.
Choose one θ*∈Θ*. Qθ has P0-density pθ/pθ*, assigned zero where pθ*=0; Qθ is unnormalized and its mass may be infinite. Test errors are nonnegative integrals under its product measure.
The sufficient consistency criterion requires test statistics converging to zero almost surely and an eventual uniform exponential type-II bound; type-I expectations need not be summable.

The compact test construction assumes a unique finite KL minimizer, finite likelihood-ratio means, and continuity at each alternative of the specified fractional moments. Its integrand is zero where pθ=0 and infinite where pθ>0 but pθ1=0, outside the null denominator exception.
The random walk starts at S0=0 and uses increments indexed n≥1; integrability, zero mean, and P(X1=0)<1 are all required.

load_bearing.statement: Let Πε have positive mass on the measurable relative KL neighborhood Bε, with P0-integrable log likelihood ratios for Π-almost every θ∈Bε. For Dn=∫Θ∏i=1ⁿ(pθ(Xi)/pθ*(Xi))Π(dθ), every α>ε satisfies Dn≥exp(−nα) eventually P0-almost surely. Under the stated jointly measurable dominated model, Dn is also finite and positive P0ⁿ-almost surely for each n.
For measurable V⊆Θ, positive prior mass on Bε, tests φn→0 P0∞-almost surely, and supθ∈V Qθⁿ(1−φn)≤exp(−nβ) eventually with β>ε imply Π(V|X1,…,Xn)→0 P0∞-almost surely.
Under the likelihood-tilt setup, for each θ and integer n≥1, the sigma-finite product measure Qθⁿ exists and has density ∏i=1ⁿrθ(xi) relative to P0ⁿ, with ratios zero where pθ*=0.
Under the hypotheses and conventions of def-likelihood-tilted-measure-at-kl-projection, each Qθ is a sigma-finite measure; Qθ*(𝒳)=1 for the selected minimizer.
Let (Xn)n≥1 be IID real random variables with E|X1|<∞, EX1=0, and P(X1=0)<1. Put S0=0 and Sn=∑i=1ⁿXi. Then P(supn≥0 Sn=+∞)=1. In particular, limsupn→∞ Sn=+∞ almost surely.

Under the stated jointly measurable dominated IID model, finite attained KL minimum, positive prior mass and log-integrability on every relative KL neighborhood, if for every η>0 there are tests φn→0 almost surely and βη>0 with supθ:d(θ,Θ*)>η Qθⁿ(1−φn)≤exp(−nβη) eventually, then Π{θ:d(θ,Θ*)>η|X1,…,Xn}→0 almost surely for every fixed η>0.

alerts.finding: thm-finite-union-bound states 'For every finite family of events' but its Facts & Assumptions begins '**Given:** A finite probability space'. Its proof step 2.1 cites L1 and L2, whose suppliers lem-finite-probability-basic-laws and thm-finite-additivity-of-probability both explicitly assume a finite probability space. Thus the supplied proof establishes a narrower domain than the unqualified Statement. Batch 12's cex-weak-tilted-tests-do-not-imply-almost-sure-consistency, step 2.1, uses this result for continuously distributed observations. The general union bound is true and follows immediately from general measure monotonicity and finite additivity, but those are not the cited suppliers here.
